analysis.investment_thesis: CMS Info Systems is a good-quality capital-light business earning ~24% ROIC at a borderline-attractive earnings yield of ~12%, placing it in the second tier of Magic Formula candidates — not cheap enough to be a screaming buy, but quality warrants holding. The 7-year net profit CAGR of 24.6% is impressive, but slowing EBITDA growth and 0% promoter stake limit conviction.
key_strengths: High ROIC (~27% EBIT/Capital Employed) sustained over multiple years — the hallmark of a good Magic Formula business
Asset-light economics: 90.7% gross margin, low D/E of 0.10, and strong OCF of INR 483 Cr in FY2025
Net profit CAGR of 24.6% over 7 years with consistent positive free cash flow (5/5 years)
key_risks: Zero promoter holding is a serious corporate governance flag — no skin-in-the-game owner-operator
EBITDA declined FY2024→FY2025 (717→649 Cr) despite revenue growth — margin compression is a red flag
Structural headwind: India's digital payments shift (UPI) threatens long-term ATM cash management volumes
red_flags: 0% promoter shareholding — no controlling owner with aligned incentives
EBITDA compressed by INR 68 Cr year-over-year in FY2025 — first reversal in the trend
CWIP surged to INR 142 Cr in FY2025 (from INR 18 Cr) and new borrowings of INR 223 Cr appeared — elevated capex cycle beginning
analysis.detailed_analysis:
**Magic Formula metrics:** EBIT FY2025 = INR 627 Cr. Enterprise Value = Market Cap (5,243.5) + Total Debt (190) − Cash (231) = ~INR 5,203 Cr, giving an Earnings Yield of 12.1% — right at the attractive threshold but not compelling. ROIC using EBIT / (Equity + Debt − Cash) ≈ 627 / 2,292 = 27.4%, which is excellent. ROCE reported at 23.7% corroborates this. The business clearly earns high returns on invested capital and trades at a barely-acceptable price — solid but not a top-decile Magic Formula rank.

**Business quality and concerns:** The 7-year operating income CAGR of 23% is impressive, but the FY2025 data shows a clear deceleration: revenue grew ~7% while EBITDA fell ~9% (717→649 Cr), suggesting cost inflation in the physical cash logistics network. The CWIP jump to INR 142 Cr and new long-term borrowings signal an upcoming capex cycle that may depress FCF. The zero promoter stake — a legacy of Blackstone's PE exit — remains the single biggest governance concern for a Greenblatt-style systematic buyer, who typically avoids businesses with no principal-agent alignment at the top.
